title: Measuring AI involvement in a repository: the epiworld case
text: ai_classify() deliberately parsimonious: catches AI involvement visible (bot identities, attribution trailers, mentions). Undisclosed AI assistance–e.g., code written editor completions committed human identity–detectable API metadata alone, figures lower bounds. Net lines changed rough proxy project size; includes documentation data files unless filtered (use file-level output gh_commit_lines() ). gh_traffic() (clones/views) covers last 14 days requires push access, building long download history requires periodic snapshots.

what: Measure the Effects of AI Coding Using the GitHub API
title: Measure the Effects of AI Coding Using the GitHub API
text: aitracking lightweight R pipeline measure effects AI-assisted coding software projects using GitHub REST API. retrieves commit histories (lines added/deleted), issue pull request conversations, download/clone statistics, evolution project’s size; classifies events involved AI coding agent; visualizes result. Design goals: Minimal dependencies. GitHub API client written base R connections; hard dependencies data.table jsonlite. Pipe-friendly. Every function takes data first argument returns data.table, steps compose R’s native pipe |>. Parsimonious AI detection. small, transparent set rules (author/committer identities, Co-authored-:/Generated trailers, @-mentions) flags AI involvement. Extend patterns.

title: Find a GitHub API token — gh_token
code: gh_token(token = NULL)

title: Find a GitHub API token — gh_token
text: token Optional character scalar. non-empty, returned -.

title: Find a GitHub API token — gh_token
text: character scalar token, empty string "" token found (requests go unauthenticated).

title: Find a GitHub API token — gh_token
text: API-calling functions aitracking take token argument defaults gh_token(), setups authentication "just works": either GITHUB_PAT/GITHUB_TOKEN set, token available git credential store. Unauthenticated requests possible heavily rate-limited GitHub (60 requests/hour versus 5,000/hour token).

title: Find a GitHub API token — gh_token
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ gh_token() # What token would be used? } # }

what: Retrieve repository traffic (clones or views) — gh_traffic
title: Retrieve repository traffic (clones or views) — gh_traffic
text: Downloads clone view history one repositories GitHub's traffic API.

title: Retrieve repository traffic (clones or views) — gh_traffic
code: gh_traffic(   repo,   metric = c("clones", "views"),   per = c("day", "week"),   token = gh_token() )

title: Retrieve repository traffic (clones or views) — gh_traffic
text: repo Character vector repositories "owner/repo" form. metric Either "clones" (default) "views". per Either "day" (default) "week". token GitHub token (see gh_token()). Note traffic API requires push access repository.

title: Retrieve repository traffic (clones or views) — gh_traffic
text: data.table columns repo, date (POSIXct, UTC), count, uniques.

title: Retrieve repository traffic (clones or views) — gh_traffic
text: GitHub stores traffic data last 14 days, building longer clone history requires periodic snapshots (e.g., scheduled GitHub Action appends output function file). download counts release assets–GitHub keep indefinitely–see gh_downloads().

title: Retrieve repository traffic (clones or views) — gh_traffic
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ gh_traffic("UofUEpiBio/epiworld") # clones, last 14 days gh_traffic("UofUEpiBio/epiworld", metric = "views", per = "week") } # }

what: Evolution of project size (lines of code) over time — loc_evolution
title: Evolution of project size (lines of code) over time — loc_evolution
text: Computes cumulative net lines code (additions minus deletions) project time commit history. file-level input (gh_commit_lines(x, files = TRUE)), evolution broken language, mapped file extensions.

title: Evolution of project size (lines of code) over time — loc_evolution
code: loc_evolution(x)

title: Evolution of project size (lines of code) over time — loc_evolution
text: x data.frame/data.table columns date, additions, deletions–.e., output gh_commit_lines(). file column present (gh_commit_lines(files = TRUE)), result computed language.

title: Evolution of project size (lines of code) over time — loc_evolution
text: data.table columns repo, date, delta (net lines changed time), loc (cumulative net lines), plus language x file-level detail. Sorted time within repo (language).

title: Evolution of project size (lines of code) over time — loc_evolution
text: measure approximate: counts net lines changed reported GitHub, includes documentation, data, non-code files (unless filter beforehand). Commits missing statistics contribute zero.

title: Evolution of project size (lines of code) over time — loc_evolution
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ gh_commits("UofUEpiBio/epiworld") |>   gh_commit_lines(files = TRUE) |>   loc_evolution() } # }

what: Plot a timeline of project activity — plot_timeline
title: Plot a timeline of project activity — plot_timeline
text: Visualizes activity project time one two ways: number commits (= "commits") lines added/deleted (= "lines"). input ai_classify(), commit bars split human AI contributions.

title: Plot a timeline of project activity — plot_timeline
code: plot_timeline(   x,   by = c("commits", "lines"),   interval = c("month", "week", "day"),   main = NULL,   col = NULL,   legend_pos = "topleft",   las = 2L,   ... )

title: Plot a timeline of project activity — plot_timeline
text: x data.frame/data.table date column (POSIXct), typically output gh_commits(), gh_commit_lines(), ai_classify(). = "lines", columns additions deletions required (see gh_commit_lines()). Either "commits" (default) "lines". interval Time bin: "month" (default), "week", "day". main Plot title. sensible default used NULL. col Bar colors. Defaults: gray/red (human/AI) commits, blue/red (added/deleted) lines. legend_pos Position legend (see graphics::legend()), NULL suppress . las Orientation axis labels (see graphics::par()). ... arguments passed graphics::barplot().

title: Plot a timeline of project activity — plot_timeline
text: x, invisibly, function can used mid-pipe.

title: Plot a timeline of project activity — plot_timeline
code: data(epiworld_commits)  epiworld_commits |>   ai_classify() |>   plot_timeline(by = "commits")   epiworld_commits |>   plot_timeline(by = "lines")

title: aitracking 0.1.0
text: GitHub REST API access base R connections (gh_api(), gh_token()). Commit history retrieval per-commit line counts (gh_commits(), gh_commit_lines()). Traffic, release-download, interaction, language retrieval (gh_traffic(), gh_downloads(), gh_interactions(), gh_languages()). Rule-based AI-involvement classification (ai_classify(), ai_patterns()). Project size evolution (loc_evolution()) activity timelines (plot_timeline()). Example datasets UofUEpiBio/epiworld C++ library.
